Tom Allen was described as the veteran ex-champion heavy-weight of America, and as the retired heavy-weight champion of this city, in March 1892.

Tom Allen and Joe Goss were to meet at Cincinnati on 12 May 1876 to draw up articles for their fight, and signed articles for the championship of the world that day at Eph Holland's Empire Saloon; Goss said Allen had authorized William Allen of Cincinnati to make the match, and the fight was to take place a fixed time after the articles were signed.

Tom Allen was one of Edwards' seconds in Edwards' fight with Collyer near Pittsburg in August 1874; he was struck with a rock before the fight but received no damage from it, and returned to St. Louis on August 15, 1874.
An estate inventory of Tom Allen's property, dated 28 July 1903, listed a champion's cup and shade, a barrel of whisky, the old piano used at concerts at his saloon and other goods.
Tom Allen fought Jem Mace at New Orleans on May 10, 1870, and was injured in the fight; Joe Coburn and Sherman Thurston seconded him.

Tom Allen went to New Orleans in May 1870 to engage Jem Mace, with Joe Coburn expected to travel with him, fought Mace there on May 10, 1870 and was injured, and returned to St. Louis on May 23 with Mace's agent Abrahams; Coburn and Sherman Thurston seconded him in the fight.
Public Administrator Garrard Strode took charge of the estate of Thomas Allen, the late saloonkeeper and former prize fighter, on April 8, 1903; it was in a muddled condition.
Public Administrator Garrard Strode took charge of Tom Allen's estate in April 1903, which was in a muddled condition, after Attorney Simon S. Bass, named as executor in Allen's will, refused to act.
Fred Watkins backed Tom Allen in his big fights, including when Allen was champion pugilist of the world, and was a lifelong friend of his.
Stakes for the Mike McCoole and Tom Allen match were put up at Tom Allen's saloon on the night of 9 October 1869 before a large crowd, with Allen and Jim Coyne said to be present.

Tom Allen was to give an exhibition in Kansas City in November 1873 with Arthur Chambers and Jack Madden; he arrived there on November 3, 1873 with Chambers, worked near Omaha, and left Omaha for Kansas City on November 21 after Omaha men threatened to shoot him and Jack Looney.

In August 1870 Tom Allen backed Punch Morris in a $100-a-side fight against Steve O'Donnell, made up at Allen's saloon on Saturday 6 August 1870 with the forfeit money put up there; Morris was quartered at the Wash Home to be trained by Allen's trainer.
Tom Allen beat Mike McCoole on 23 September 1873, regaining the heavyweight title, and a knuckle on his right hand was slightly cut.
Tom Allen beat Mike McCoole on 23 September 1873, regaining the heavyweight title; Arthur Chambers and Patsy Shepherd were among his seconds, and a knuckle on his right hand was slightly cut.
Tom Allen was in a street fight with Dan Daly at Seventh and Market streets, St. Louis, on June 17, 1888, after he tried to invade Daly's saloon; Daly whipped him.
Tom Allen's brother Harry Allen was matched to fight Joe Goss for the championship of England on September 4, 1868, but the fight never came off; Harry died soon after the planned fight was stopped.
Tom Allen's brother Harry Allen was matched to fight Joe Goss for the championship of England on September 4, 1868, but police arrested Harry and the fight never came off; Harry died soon after.
Tom Allen learned gun-making and then entered the English army during the Crimean War, where his success in turn-ups in front of Sevastopol convinced him he could be a champion.
